one_line: Khalsa commander who led the first Sikh state and land reforms in early 18th-century Punjab.

appearance.age_look: Early 30s to mid-30s, lean but strong, with the wiry build of a campaign-hardened rider.
appearance.face: Oval face with high cheekbones, wheatish-brown North Indian complexion, straight nose, intense dark-brown eyes under slightly arched brows, a neatly kept full beard, and a calm yet resolute default expression that hints at stern determination.
appearance.hair: Uncut black hair tied in a compact topknot under a deep navy-blue domed Sikh-style turban (early 18th-century dastar) with a slightly forward tilt, wrapped smooth with a thin mustard-yellow turban band near the base and a small steel khanda emblem at the front.
appearance.costume: He wears an early 18th-century Khalsa warrior outfit: a long knee-length deep saffron angarkha-style kurta with wrap-over front and side ties, fitted full sleeves, and a subtle woven stripe texture; over it a sleeveless dark indigo-blue quilted char-aina-style padded coat for light armour, cinched with a broad brown leather belt with a simple steel buckle; loose white cotton churidar trousers gathered at the ankles, and sturdy brown leather riding boots that cover the shins; across his chest runs a diagonal dark-brown leather strap holding a small round steel shield on his back; he has a plain steel kara on his right wrist and a simple cloth kamarband (sash) in muted maroon tied over the belt with its ends tucked neatly, no excessive ornamentation to keep him austere yet martial.
appearance.signature: A slightly curved Sikh warrior talwar with a plain steel blade, a brass hilt with a simple cross-guard, and a brown leather-wrapped grip, carried in a dark-brown leather scabbard with minimal brass fittings, worn at his left hip and often held in his right hand in a ready but controlled stance.

ref_desc: Banda Singh Bahadur is a lean, wheatish-complexioned Sikh warrior in a deep saffron angarkha, dark indigo quilted coat, white churidar, brown leather boots and belt, navy-blue turban with khanda emblem, carrying a curved steel talwar in a brown scabbard with steel kara on his wrist.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet of Banda Singh Bahadur as an early 18th-century Sikh commander: a lean, campaign-hardened man in his early thirties with a wheatish-brown complexion, oval face, intense dark-brown eyes, neatly kept full beard and a calm but resolute expression. His uncut black hair is tied in a compact topknot under a deep navy-blue domed turban with smooth wraps, a thin mustard-yellow band near the base, and a small steel khanda emblem at the front. He wears a knee-length deep saffron angarkha-style kurta with wrap-over front, fitted sleeves and subtle woven stripe texture, over which sits a sleeveless dark indigo-blue quilted padded coat, cinched with a broad brown leather belt and a muted maroon cloth sash. His loose white cotton churidar trousers gather at the ankles into sturdy brown leather riding boots that cover his shins. A dark-brown leather strap crosses his chest to hold a small round steel shield on his back, and a plain steel kara circles his right wrist. At his left hip hangs his signature weapon, a slightly curved Sikh talwar with a plain steel blade, brass hilt and brown leather-wrapped grip, in a dark-brown leather scabbard with minimal brass fittings; show him also holding the unsheathed talwar in one hand in a composed, ready stance. Use a colour palette dominated by deep saffron, dark indigo blue, white, brown leather and steel grey, and present him from front and slight angle views so his face, turban, garments, boots, strap, kara and sword can be clearly redrawn consistently.
